summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling. Customer seeks to validate latency and cost for conversational + embeddings workload; discussed QPS/concurrency targets, token distribution, benchmark plan, and success criteria. Agreed next steps: share SOW, run benchmark on dedicated capacity, customer to provide traces.
topics: Benchmark plan and metrics (p95/p99 latency, throughput, cost per 1M tokens)
transcript:
[00:00] Samantha Lee: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. we've got about 60 minutes, agenda is to scope the POC around workload modeling and benchmarks. quick intros?
[00:08] Markus Jensen: Markus here, CTO at Sable Finance. Priya and Omar are with me.
[00:12] Priya Patel: hi all, Head of ML at Sable. we're building a customer-facing conversational assistant plus embeddings for search and some reranking.
[00:20] Diego Ramos: Great, Diego from Redwood, infra and perf lead. we'll focus on QPS, concurrency, token distributions, and what success looks like.
[00:28] Omar Khan: Omar, platform. main constraint is we need predictable latency during peak trading hours, and data residency in us-west.
[00:36] Samantha Lee: perfect. Markus, can you give us the expected traffic shape? average QPS, peak, concurrency?
[00:44] Markus Jensen: sure. baseline is around 8 QPS for conversational flows during normal hours, and peaks up to 60 QPS during retention windows. for the search/embeddings endpoints we see bursts, maybe 120 QPS short bursts for reindexing, but steady-state is 20 QPS. concurrency wise — roughly 40 concurrent generation sessions at peak, but heavy tail events could push to 80.
[01:12] Priya Patel: token stats — average user message is about 80–150 input tokens, responses average 40–120 tokens. embedding calls are small, input texts about 200 tokens average. across flows weighted average input tokens ~120, output ~60.
[01:30] Diego Ramos: that's super helpful. for planning we'd model two profiles: conversational generation (chat) and embeddings/rerank. conversational: avg QPS 8 steady, 60 peak, avg input 120 tokens, avg output 60 tokens. embeddings: steady 20 QPS, bursts to 120 for reindex, avg tokens 200.
[01:55] Samantha Lee: what are your latency expectations?
[01:58] Omar Khan: p95 we want under 350ms for generation tokens and p99 under 700ms ideally. for embeddings p95 under 50ms.
[02:08] Diego Ramos: those are tight but realistic with dedicated capacity and quantized model variants. one caveat — p95 latency numbers for autoregressive gen depend on output length and batching. we need to model per-token throughput and how batching affects tail.
[02:24] Priya Patel: can you walk through the math for per-token cost and QPS mapping to GPU throughput?
[02:30] Diego Ramos: yeah. rough formula: tokens_per_second = model_tokens_per_second on given hardware. For example a quant-llama-ish 13B on A100-style has X tps — (note: transient numbers during call) — but more practically we run benchmark jobs. for the POC we'll run a throughput sweep: increase offered QPS and measure p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens.
[02:54] Markus Jensen: we also care about concurrency vs latency tradeoffs. our app is sensitive to tail latency so batching that increases p99 is bad.
[03:02] Diego Ramos: agreed. Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching with strict SLO caps and burst policies; we can configure maximum batching delay to limit added latency. for POC we recommend two experiments: one low-latency config (batch window 10ms) and one high-efficiency config (batch window 40–60ms) to show cost/latency curves.
[03:25] Samantha Lee: timeline? how long to run meaningful benchmarks?
[03:28] Diego Ramos: typical is a 1-hour warmup + 1–2 hour sweep across QPS points, plus a 24-hour soak if you want to capture diurnal effects. for the POC standard we do 1 week: initial perf runs in week 1, integration and security review concurrently, week 2 customer validation and cost analysis, week 3 tuning and final report. so roughly 3–4 weeks end-to-end.
[03:56] Priya Patel: success criteria — what should we sign off on?
[04:00] Samantha Lee: what do you need as success criteria from Sable?
[04:03] Priya Patel: p95 latency under 350ms for chat at 60 peak QPS, throughput to sustain 60QPS with <10% error rate, embeddings p95 under 50ms at steady 20QPS, and cost target of less than $X per 1M tokens (we left X blank and will fill after pricing). also we want model quality equal to our current baseline (small diff in ROUGE/embedding recall), plus security checks passed.
[04:30] Diego Ramos: we'll measure quality using your evaluation set. we'll run A/B against your baseline model and include quality metrics in the benchmark report. for cost we'll provide modeled estimates and observed cost in the benchmark harness.
[04:44] Omar Khan: on security — we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), encryption with customer-managed KMS, VPC peering or private link.
[04:54] Samantha Lee: noted. Redwood Private can do VPC and KMS; for the hosted POC we can offer dedicated capacity in a customer-isolated cluster with KMS integration. we'll attach the SOC2 and architecture diagram.
[05:06] Priya Patel: any constraints around data retention during the POC?
[05:10] Samantha Lee: we can disable logs retention and forward only audit logs to your SIEM; full payload retention can be disabled for POC. we'll document that in the SOW.
[05:20] Markus Jensen: can you summarize what you need from us for the bench?
[05:24] Diego Ramos: yes: 1) representative traffic traces or synthetic prompt distributions (CSV with timestamps and token counts), 2) evaluation dataset for quality checks, 3) access to a staging environment or allow Redwood to run from our dedicated test cluster in us-west, 4) list of models you want us to compare.
[05:40] Priya Patel: we'll provide traces and evaluation set. model list: baseline is our current in-house 7B finetuned model, open to comparing quantized 13B and 30B variants.
[05:50] Diego Ramos: perfect. for the benchmark harness we'll parameterize by avg input tokens 120, avg output 60, conversational steady QPS 8, peak 60, embeddings steady 20 burst 120, and concurrency headroom 80. We'll generate percentiles and cost curves.
[06:10] Samantha Lee: any gotchas we should call out?
[06:13] Diego Ramos: yes — long context windows, KV cache pressure, and tokenization differences across models can skew numbers. also real-world user behavior has spikes and retries which increase effective QPS. we'll run some stress tests with retry behavior.
[06:28] Omar Khan: on telemetry, we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency. does Redwood expose that?
[06:34] Samantha Lee: yes, Redwood Console gives per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost, and trace hooks. we'll include sample screenshots in the docs.
[06:43] Markus Jensen: what's the proposed POC SOW and cost for a 4-week pilot?
[06:48] Samantha Lee: we'll send a SOW that includes 2 weeks of benchmark instrumentation and 2 weeks of tuning and validation. pricing will reflect dedicated test capacity hours and engineering support; we'll include optional dedicated reserved hours for week-of-peak testing.
[06:59] Priya Patel: fine. last question — can you run the benchmark against our on-prem infra or does Redwood need to host?
[07:05] Diego Ramos: we can run either: Redwood Dedicated in a customer-dedicated cluster hosted in your cloud region, or Redwood Private for fully customer-managed infra. for an on-prem run, we need a brief install and network setup; that's usually more time. recommended for speed: let Redwood run in a dedicated cluster we provide in us-west for the POC.
[07:24] Samantha Lee: great. recap and next steps: Samantha send SOW & SOC2, Diego schedule benchmark and send test harness, Sable to provide traces and evaluation set.
[07:34] Markus Jensen: thanks, that works.
[07:36] Samantha Lee: thanks everyone we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark kickoff. Bye.
[07:40] (call ends)
